sources.rationale: Builtin input() returns an attacker-typed line. Sources are not route-gated, so CLI tools seed from here too.

sinks.rationale: os.system passes its argument to the shell verbatim; any attacker text in it is shell syntax.
os.popen runs its command string through the shell, same exposure as os.system.
subprocess.run with a shell interprets the command string; only a literal shell=False at the call site suppresses the hit (a computed value never does).
subprocess.Popen is the constructor form of subprocess.run; same shell interpretation of the command argument.
Legacy wrapper over Popen; the command argument reaches the same shell interpretation path.
Output-capturing wrapper over Popen; the command argument reaches the same shell interpretation path.
Checked wrapper over Popen; the command argument reaches the same shell interpretation path.
DB-API 2.0 cursor.execute(sql) — the standard SQL execution surface across drivers. Name-equality match, hence heuristic confidence.
DB-API 2.0 batched execution; the statement argument is SQL text.
sqlite3 multi-statement execution; parameterisation is not available on this surface at all.
sqlalchemy.text() wraps a raw SQL fragment that the engine executes as written.
Builtin eval executes its argument as a Python expression.
Builtin exec executes its argument as Python statements.
compile() turns attacker text into a code object; execution typically follows immediately.
Builtin open with an attacker-influenced path reads or writes outside the intended directory via dot segments.
io.open is the same call as builtin open under its importable name.
Low-level file open; same traversal exposure as builtin open.
Constructing a Jinja2 template from attacker text allows template-expression execution when rendered.
Renders its first argument as a Jinja2 template in the app context — the canonical Flask SSTI surface.
Mako templates embed Python; a template built from attacker text is code execution on render.
A Django template compiled from attacker text evaluates attacker-chosen template expressions and filters.
Markup() marks its argument HTML-safe without escaping it — attacker text is then emitted raw by templates.
Re-exported markupsafe.Markup; same safe-marking of unescaped attacker text.
mark_safe exempts its argument from Django's template auto-escaping.

sanitizers.rationale: A validation-shaped guard: it does not rewrite the value and its adequacy depends on the pattern, so the flow stays alive with the sanitizer hop recorded for downstream classification.
Same validation shape as re.match; anchored, but pattern adequacy is still call-site-specific, so tag rather than kill.
literal_eval only builds literal values, so it defuses eval-style execution of the parsed TEXT — but the resulting value can still be an attacker string, so the flow is tagged, not killed.
int() returns an int object or raises; no character of the input survives into the return value, so the returned value cannot carry injection syntax for any string-consuming sink class listed.

propagators.rationale: Any tainted component survives into the joined path; a later absolute or dot-segment component can even discard the safe prefix.
POSIX-flavoured variant of os.path.join with identical propagation.
abspath normalises but does not validate — a traversal path stays attacker-chosen after normalisation.
Percent-decoding REVEALS injection characters that were encoded; the output is at least as attacker-controlled as the input.
Form-flavoured percent-decoding; same taint exposure as unquote.
Decoding is a bijection over attacker bytes; the decoded value is fully attacker-chosen.
Parsed structure and every string inside it come from the attacker document; whole-value granularity taints the result.
Codec decoding (including rot13/hex/base64 codecs) transforms attacker bytes into attacker text.
